_comment: The per-figure registry roadmap EVI-2 asked for. Each entry names the figure text it vouches for, where that figure lives in README.md (the `claim:<id>` marker beside its paragraph), what produced it, and whether a clone can re-run it. tools/check_claims.py is the lint; ci.yml runs it. Since EVI-4, every entry also carries an artifact field: null when no pipeline artifact publishes the figure (a dated local measurement has none, by disclosure), or {"name", "workflow"} naming the Actions artifact and the workflow that uploads it, which the lint verifies against .github/workflows/. No figure quoted in the README is currently produced by a pipeline artifact (the nightly gate publishes the nightly-interpolation workload, which no entry quotes), so every entry here is null until a producer plugs into the pipeline.

claims.notes: Re-measured after the word-wise bit reads and the slicing-by-16 frame CRC.
Publication is an open item with counsel before 1.0; the figure is quoted because a synthetic generator flatters it by ~2.5x.
The sketch's win is bounded work, not speed, on this workload.
Taken on a heavily loaded box (load average ~200, unpinned); ratios are shape, not a specification.
Before reduce took the integer path for values that fit.
The pre-change shipped path; kept so the ~10x cost of the BigDecimal-points path stays readable.
Server-side reduce over 1M real closes; the naive baselines in the same table are the comparison.
Hourly avg over 1M real closes, before and after the integer path.

claims.notes: One interpolate_range call; the two-decimal number is re-runnable, the real-closes number is not, so the entry as a whole is not.
Quoted as a retraction: the ~2.6x sketch advantage was an artefact of the old generator's digit count.
Observation about tokio's sleep-after-work interval, not a performance claim.
